en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Surusuru Chapter 55.
The Training Rule on Worldly Gain.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was staying among the Bhaggas at Susumāragira, in the Bhesakaḷā Grove, the Deer Park.
Now at that time, the bhikkhus were receiving the water-bowl with a hand soiled by food in the Kokanada Palace.
People complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
"How can these ascetics, followers of the Sakyan, receive a water-bowl with a hand soiled by food? They are just like householders who indulge in sensual pleasures!"
The monks heard those people grumbling, complaining, and criticizing.
Those monks who were of few desires... [and so on]... they grumbled, complained, and criticized:
"How can these monks receive a water vessel with a hand that has food on it?"... [and so on]...
“Is it true, monks, that monks receive a water bowl with a hand soiled by food?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before]...
"How indeed, monks, can those foolish men receive a water vessel with a hand soiled by food?
This, monks, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:"
“The training is to be observed: ‘I will not accept a drinking vessel with a hand that has food on it.
A drinking vessel must not be accepted with a hand that has food on it.
Whoever, out of disrespect, accepts a drinking vessel with a hand that has food on it, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).”
There is no offense if it was unintentional,
or if there was a lack of mindfulness.
If one accepts it from someone who is unaware or from someone who is ill,
thinking, "I will wash it," or "I will have it washed," [there is no offense].
In times of distress,
for one who is insane,
and for the first offender.
The fifth training rule is concluded.
